explanation: Count each distinct character, then recursively extend a prefix with any character whose remaining count is positive. Decrement before recursion and restore after it so sibling choices see the original counts.
correctness: Each recursive state has used exactly the prefix multiset and retains exactly the unused occurrences. Choosing a positive-count character preserves this invariant; reaching full length uses every occurrence. Every distinct target string determines one available next-character choice at each level, so all and only distinct permutations are reached.
walkthrough: For ab, counts start as {a:1,b:1}. Choose a, leaving only b and emitting ab; restore the counts. Choose b, leaving only a and emitting ba. For aa, there is only one available character choice at either level, so aa is emitted once. Empty input immediately emits the empty string. Return a set of strings; the adapter displays a JSON array and compares membership without imposing output order.
edgeCases: repeated characters under the bank extension.
Empty input returns the singleton set {""}; repeated characters yield distinct strings only, not repeated output entries.
timeComplexity: Expected O(n*n!) worst-case time: with distinct characters there are n! output strings, each constructed/hashed in O(n); all smaller recursion levels are dominated by this bound.
spaceComplexity: O(n*n!) worst-case output storage. Outside the output, the count map and recursion depth are O(n); immutable prefixes retained along a recursion path can total O(n²) characters.
